claim: For integers \(p\ge1\) and \(m\ge0\), let \(\mathcal L_{p,m}=\{a^{m+kp}:k\ge0\}\) over the unary alphabet \(\{a\}\). Among \(\varepsilon\)-free NFAs with one initial state, every transition crossing a fixed bipartition, and simple undirected transition graph a cactus, the exact minimum number of states is \(\max\{\ell,m+\ell-p+1\}\), where \(\ell=\operatorname{lcm}(p,2)\).

scientific_limitations_and_integrity.integrity: The result is supported by an explicit lower bound, a matching construction, and reproducible bounded checks; bibliographic novelty is not asserted beyond the documented comparisons.
limitations: No claim is made for several accepted residues, non-unary alphabets, epsilon transitions, or automata without the bipartition constraint.
The finite construction checks corroborate the witness only; the universal minimum follows from the written proof.
No independent audit or independent validation is claimed.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.scope: Unary arithmetic-progression languages with one initial state, no epsilon transitions, a transition-compatible bipartition, and a simple undirected cactus transition graph.

title: Exact state cost of thresholded unary residue languages in bipartite-cactus NFAs
